Indian Standard SPECIFICATION FOR CRANK SHAFT FOR JUTE LOOMS
O. FORE W 0 R D
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 9 March 1988, after the draft finalized by the Jute Mill Machinery/Accessories and Spare Parts Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been formulated with a view to providing guidance to manufacturers and users of crank shaft for jute looms. This standard would ensure manufacture of crank shafts of acceptable quality leading to improved functioning of the jute looms, 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960-. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

-Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ),

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of crank shaft used in jute looms.

and journals of the crank shaft shall be smooth finished and polished. The roughness value (R. ) of crank pins and the journals shall be within 1'6 to 6'3 (.Lm. 3.3 Co-altiality and Parallelism - While manufacturing the crank shaft, the co-axiality of journals and crank pins and parallelism between the axis of the journals and the crank pins should be maintained.

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.0 For the purpose of this standard, following definitions shall apply . 2.1 Left-Hand Loom - A loom starting handle on its left hand side, with the the the

4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Dimensions
4.1.1 Nominal - The nominal dimensions of the crank shaft shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the manufacturer. In the absence of any agreement, these shall be as declared by the manufacturer, 4.1.2 Tolerance - The nominal dimensions ( set Fig. I ) shall be subject to the following tolerances in millimetres:
A

2.2 Right-Hand Loom - A loom with starting handle on its right hand side.

NOTE - If an obser ver stands near the d eli very end of the loom and looks against the run of the warp , the sid e on his left-hand is left-hand side of th e loom and the sid e on his right hand is the right-hand side of the loom.

2.3 Reed Space ( of the Loom) - Maxim urn space available on loom for the insertion of a reed, that is, the overall width of the reed which can be fixed on the loom . 2.4 Crank Radius - The perpendicular distance between the axis of the crank shaft journal and the axis of its crank pin.

3. MANUFACTURE
3.1 Material - Crank shaft shall be manufactured from carbon steel bars conforming to Class 2A of IS : 1875-1978-. 3.2 Workmanship and Finish -The shaft shall be straight and free from rust. Crank pin

4.2 True RUDIling - The journals and crank pins of the crank shaft shan run true. However, when tested by the method given in A-I, outof-true running of journals and the crank pins, if present, shall not exceed 0'025 and 0'013 mm, respectively. 4.3 Parallelism - Each of the crank pins shall be parallel to both the journals. However, when tested by the method given in A-2, a deviation of 0'05 mm from parallelism shall be permitted. 4.4 Crank Radius - The variation in crank radius of the crank shaft when tested by the method given in A-3, shall not exceed 0'2 mm. 4.5 Dynamic Balancing - The central portion of the crank shaft shall have machined surface for achieving dynamic balancing.

6. PACKING
6.1 The crank shaft shall be coated lightly with rust preventive grease and sh all be held in semicircular slots cut out in fou r parallel wooden planks fixed in vertical position inside a wooden case. The slots should be suitably protected so that wood does not come in direct contact with the shaft. The wooden case shall be strong enough to withstand the hazards of transit.
6.2 Each case shall be marked with the following information:
a) Manufacturer's name, initials and trademark, if any; b) Reed space of the loom on which the crank shafts are to be used; c) 'R' or 'L' depending upon the right-hand or left-hand loom on which the crank shaft is to be used; and d ) Number of crank shafts in the case.

5. MARKING
5.1 Each crank shaft shall be marked, at a suitable place, with the following:
a) Reed space of the loom on which it is to be used, and b) 'R' or 'L' depending upon the right-hand or left-hand loom on which it is to be used.

5.1.1 Each crank shaft rna y also be marked with the Standard Mark.
NOT. - The use of the Standard Mark is g overned b y the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards
